_schema: testId, environment, procedure, expectedResult, observedResult, status, evidenceRef, operatorNotes

automated.procedure: CASE A (normal exit -> restart) and CASE C (real kill -9 forced termination -> restart), reproduced this phase against the freshly-rebuilt Linux binary
automated.expectedResult: 0 migrations on second launch, BSB already present (0 re-imported), no stale Active presentation, no panics
automated.observedResult: PASS - see ../software/xvfb-relaunch-3.4-run1-fresh.log and ../software/xvfb-relaunch-3.4-run2-idempotent.log; Phase 3.2/3.3 already produced real SIGKILL evidence (exit code 137) against an earlier build of this same binary and it is not re-fabricated here
automated.operatorNotes: Strongest crash-recovery evidence obtainable without real hardware - still Environment B, not C.

automated.procedure: VACUUM INTO backup + simulated working-database loss + restore round-trip test
automated.observedResult: PASS - unchanged this phase, re-verified in full regression re-run

realHardwareRequired.procedure: CASE B: presentation active -> application closed normally -> restart, on the real target machine
realHardwareRequired.expectedResult: No stale Active presentation, no crash

realHardwareRequired.procedure: CASE C: presentation active -> forced process termination (Task Manager 'End Task') -> restart, on the real target machine
realHardwareRequired.expectedResult: No database corruption, no stale Active presentation
realHardwareRequired.operatorNotes: Environment B already proved this with a real kill -9 on Linux (REC-A-01) - a real Windows equivalent (End Task / taskkill) has not been performed.

realHardwareRequired.procedure: CASE D: during audio capture -> application failure/restart
realHardwareRequired.expectedResult: No lost service data, operator receives understandable status

realHardwareRequired.procedure: CASE E: during a database operation -> restart
CASE F: backup -> intentionally replace the working database (on an isolated pilot/test database, with an explicit prior backup, never production data) -> restore -> reopen
realHardwareRequired.expectedResult: No data loss, no duplicate BSB data
realHardwareRequired.operatorNotes: Environment A already proved the restore mechanism itself works (REC-A-02) - only its execution on the real target machine's real filesystem/OS is BLOCKED.
